events.summary: Drones launched from Iraqi territory struck Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline on Sep. 11. Saudi Arabia subsequently shut the line. Launch origin is established at country/territory level; perpetrator identity and Iranian command are not.

Iraq removed the Maysan operations commander and later the provincial police chief, while transferring or referring additional security officials for investigation after confirming Iraqi territorial origin of the Saudi-bound drone attacks.

Iraq temporarily closed multiple Iran-border crossings and the al-Tayyib border area while searching for perpetrators and launch sites. Crossing status changed during the day, including humanitarian passage.

Iraqi Security Media Cell said an intelligence and security task force located and seized a launch platform inside Iraq used in the incident targeting the Saudi pipeline; forensic and technical examination remained underway.

Iraq said it approved an Iranian request to participate in or closely monitor the investigation into the Saudi pipeline attack and seized launch-platform evidence. This participation does not establish Iranian responsibility for the attack.

Yemeni government-aligned forces reported drone or air strikes on Houthi positions in Al-Dhale and on weapons, ammunition and missile convoys moving from Mocha toward Sanaa in Taiz. Battle-damage effects were not independently established.
Saudi Civil Defense said a Houthi projectile fell in Al-Tuwal, Jazan, injuring two people and damaging a mosque, buildings and vehicles.

President Donald Trump said the Houthis contacted his administration and indicated they preferred that the United States not become directly involved in the Yemen conflict. The reported contact is preserved as Trump's account, not as an independently published Houthi ultimatum.

BRICS adopted the New Delhi Declaration, urging maximum restraint and diplomacy in the Middle East and advancing voluntary technical insurance and reinsurance cooperation. The final text did not establish the Iran-proposed $10 billion BRICS reinsurer.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed on the BRICS sidelines. Public readouts emphasized de-escalation, stability, peace and development; no concrete maritime, sanctions or trade bargain was announced.

An Iranian commercial vessel was reported struck near Qeshm/Hengam, with fire, crew evacuation and casualties. UKMTO separately reported a projectile strike; the record does not assume the reports describe the same vessel, and attribution remains unresolved.

Xi Jinping proposed deeper Greater BRICS practical cooperation, including an AI Open Source Zone, a BRICS Special Economic Zone partnership and a 2027 Service Trade Forum. No Iran-specific wartime financial commitment was established in this proposal.

record.evidence: Later Saudi and Iraqi reporting established that drones launched from Iraqi territory struck the East-West pipeline and that Saudi Arabia shut the line. Earlier unresolved smoke observation remains preserved as prior state.
Later Reuters reporting and multiple Yemeni government sources confirmed Houthi seizure of Perim/Mayun. This is an update to the Sep. 11 occurrence, not a Sep. 12 capture.
The final New Delhi Declaration supports generic BRICS insurance/reinsurance resilience mechanisms but does not establish the reported Iran-specific $10 billion reinsurer.

record.topic: Cause of smoke observed near Saudi East-West pipeline south of Medina
record.resolution: Later evidence establishes an Iraqi-origin drone attack on the East-West pipeline and Saudi shutdown. Perpetrator identity, exact damaged facilities and official repair timeline remain unresolved.

record.topic: Scope of direct IRGC operational guidance to Houthi forces
record.evidence: Reuters Sep. 12 reiterated direct IRGC guidance for the west-coast offensive while Iran continued to deny military direction. This strengthens evidence of guidance for that offensive but does not establish IRGC command over every Houthi operation.

record.topic: Announced future U.S. sanction on an unnamed large bank
record.rule: Do not convert the Sep. 10 announcement into completed legal action before OFAC enactment.
record.evidence: No OFAC enactment or reliable bank identification was established by the Sep. 13 noon evidence cutoff.

record.topic: Exact East-West pipeline facilities damaged and official repair timeline
record.evidence: Shutdown confirmed; satellite damage/smoke and industry repair estimates exist, but official facility-level BDA and repair duration remain limited.

record.topic: Who ordered or conducted the Saudi East-West pipeline attack
record.evidence: Launch origin is narrowed to Iraq/Maysan. No responsible group is established; Iraqi-origin evidence does not establish Iranian command.

record.topic: What Oman has actually agreed to on Hormuz routes, fees, sovereignty and reopening
record.evidence: Iranian sources describe an understanding and evolving conditions; no matching Omani public confirmation was found by cutoff.

record.topic: What are the seven conditions Iran says it transmitted to the United States
record.evidence: Actor media report seven conditions with top-leadership approval; details were not publicly enumerated in the reviewed report.

record.topic: Who struck the Iranian commercial vessel near Qeshm/Hengam
record.evidence: Event and casualties are reported; attribution remains unresolved, and the UKMTO projectile report is not conclusively matched to the Iranian report.

record.topic: Whether the Sep. 12 Iran-UAE meeting produced a concrete bargain
record.evidence: Only general de-escalation and stability readouts are established; no specific embargo relief, maritime guarantee or quid pro quo was announced.

record.topic: Whether Houthis can sustain control and anti-shipping capability from Perim/Mayun
record.evidence: Capture is established and counterstrikes are underway; durable control and deployed maritime fires are not established.

record.topic: Scope and integrity implications of Iranian participation in the Iraqi inquiry
record.evidence: Iraq says Iranian participation or close monitoring was approved; access, team composition and chain-of-custody scope remain unspecified.

record.disposition: Saudi Arabia shut the East-West pipeline after the Iraqi-origin drone attack. Exact damaged facilities and official repair duration remained unresolved; Reuters industry estimates ranged from days to as long as five to six weeks, with possible partial restart during repairs.
Projectile strike/fire and crew evacuation were reported. The exact vessel identity and attribution remained unresolved.

record.note: Iran reported one killed and four wounded; early AP variants carried three or four wounded. Current canonical status retains the later four-wounded report while preserving the reporting evolution.

record.claim: Iran was probably responsible for the Saudi East-West pipeline attack.
record.evidence_note: Iraqi launch origin is established; Iranian command is not.

record.claim: The Iran-Oman understanding is a step toward Iran exercising sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz and does not itself reopen the strait.
record.evidence_note: Preserve as Iranian negotiating position, not agreed legal status.

record.metric: Saudi crude export capacity at risk
record.observed_state: The East-West pipeline had been rerouting about 4 million bpd to Yanbu. Reuters sources said Yanbu stocks could maintain exports for roughly 5-7 days without restart; up to about 4% of global supply could then be jeopardized.
Saudi Arabia had not published an official repair timeline. Reuters industry sources ranged from days to as long as five to six weeks, with possible partial restart during repairs.
Reuters reported another all-time high above $6.20 per gallon on Sep. 13 amid regional energy disruption.

The final declaration supports a self-reliant BRICS insurance ecosystem, further reinsurance-capacity discussion, a voluntary Insurance Resilience Centre concept and an India-hosted Risk Lab open to interested members. It does not establish an Iran-specific $10 billion reinsurer.
Still pending by noon Sep. 13; the bank and country were not reliably identified and no OFAC enactment was established.
Reuters reported the Saudi benchmark down 1.3% on Sunday after pipeline and regional attacks, with Aramco down 1.6%.
Projectile strike, fire, crew evacuation and Iranian casualties reported near Qeshm/Hengam; attribution unresolved and UKMTO/IRAN report identity match not assumed.
Later reporting confirms Houthi seizure of Perim/Mayun, materially increasing the group's geographic position at Bab el-Mandeb; physical closure of the strait is not established.
Houthi spokesman said navigation remained safe except Saudi vessels under their announced ban; this is an actor claim, not an independent safety assessment.

Iranian sources said the prospective Oman understanding would not itself reopen Hormuz, reopening depends on U.S. conditions, and Iran seeks authority and fees. Iran also said no signed deal was expected at the Monday meeting. No matching Omani public confirmation was established by the noon cutoff.
A broad set of Arab and Islamic governments and organizations condemned the East-West pipeline attack and affirmed Saudi sovereignty and security.
The UK foreign secretary expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and support for its right to defend itself while emphasizing freedom of navigation.
